briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: New Storefronts, New Momentum: Ann Arbor Opens Doors as DC Moves Toward Rescheduling
briefs.top: Michigan operators got a fresh reason to smile as New Standard's Ann Arbor storefront threw open its doors this month, even as the 24% wholesale tax fight heads toward real legal and electoral turning points. Nationally, the DEA has now gone on record arguing for Schedule III while the FDA gears up for a landmark psychedelics hearing next week — signs the federal ground is shifting in the industry's favor.

local.text: New Standard's Ann Arbor dispensary threw open its doors with an opening-weekend blitz of giveaways and discounts running September 3-6, giving Washtenaw County shoppers another premium option and operators a fresh proof point that new store launches still pencil out.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary is pushing ahead with an ambitious hospitality-driven dispensary-restaurant buildout, a sign that operators with the right concept and capital are still expanding even as the wholesale tax squeezes weaker competitors out of rural markets.

Republican gubernatorial nominee John James is campaigning on slashing Michigan's cannabis tax burden, unveiling a "Freedom Agenda" plank arguing the levy "drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections" — putting real tax relief on the November ballot for operators.

The 24% wholesale tax generated roughly $37 million in Q2 and $34 million in Q1 — a fraction of the $105 million per quarter state officials projected, ammunition operators and the bipartisan repeal push in Lansing are already using to argue the tax is failing on its own terms.

The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's original lawsuit challenging the wholesale tax is now heading to a September trial, while a second lawsuit filed against Treasury keeps the legal pressure on — giving operators two live paths toward getting the tax struck down and back-taxes reimbursed.

national.text: FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research just previewed its approach in the New England Journal of Medicine, with CDER's new permanent director and top psychiatry officials touting the agency's newly finalized guidance as offering developers of psilocybin, MDMA and LSD-derived therapies a flexible, science-driven path forward ahead of a public hearing on therapeutic psychedelic use next week.

DEA's own final post-hearing brief now argues marijuana no longer meets the criteria to stay in Schedule I, and a D.C. Circuit ruling on the legality of the administration's Schedule III move is expected imminently — with billions in tax benefits for licensed operators hanging on the outcome.

Curaleaf's $4-per-share, 45%-premium takeover bid for Canada's Aurora Cannabis is now formally underway, a cross-border deal that would create a combined company with more than $1.5 billion in pro forma revenue and a template other major MSOs are watching closely.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy COMP360 showed six-month durability in treatment-resistant depression trials and remains on track for a Q4 2026 FDA New Drug Application, with commercial launch targeted for the first half of 2027.

Congress bought the hemp industry breathing room, with President Trump signing a bill pushing the federal ban on hemp-derived THC products from November 12 back to December 11, giving operators and lawmakers more runway to negotiate real regulatory guardrails instead of an outright ban.
